utterances.text: Did this mean that there were no contacts whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: No, of course not, because of the situation that we were all in, this could not have passed without any contacts. I think the Prosecutor found a very nice formulation for that [B/C/S spoken] tensions were present, if this is the proper way to translate it into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned earlier that this delegation that was going to Srebrenica submitted a report. Were you thinking about the government delegation, the working group that you sent to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter 17324 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, this is the document I believe that you did not admit. It was open to Mr. Karadzic to elicit further information on this document in direct and then we would have been able to cross-examine on it. It's impermissible for him now to seek to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. President, we were not going to tender it until it came up in cross-examination since she started asking him about the information he had received, and he mentioned, in fact, during his cross-examination about the commission that had gone to Srebrenica. So now we think that it's appropriate to use it. If she has some recross-examination on it, you can permit that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask to zoom in on the page in Serbian, if the English version is available to other participants on their screens so that Mr. Kozic, the then-prime minister, could tell us whether this was the report and what it contains. May I help you? It says that the visit took place on the 16th; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, right. I'm just reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A state of war was declared?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Correct. And the War Presidency was set up, the duties and tasks were formulated to clear up the town, remove the bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Kozic. All you asked to the witness before putting this document was you referred -- it's just whether he referred to a working group. It does not open you to ask any content about it. So why don't you put some foundational question about it to the witness. The witness himself in the statement, he did not know well about the contents. So what is your question to the witness, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that he did not mean this one because today during cross-examination the witness said that the government working group submitted a report about the situation and about the removal. He said something from the contents of this document, about the clearing up of the town, and so on. He said -- he mentioned a part of the contents of the document during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we find out the passage?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I believe that's page 84, line 2.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see this report of the working group, and did the working group implement what you requested it to do in terms of the report and the proposed measures?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Of course. And we acted in accordance with that, as I said earlier. When asked by the Prosecutor, I did mention some of these details, what they did and I said that the report was submitted and adopted and then it was implemented or we acted in accordance with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this is more about Serbs who died, on page 84. I think it's later on. I will find it. Just -- I ask for your indulgence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't find it now. But the witness has confirmed that he spontaneously mentioned the work, or rather, the report of this commission. Can you accept that and admit the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the witness made any further comment than those made in the statement. Mr. Robinson, could you assist us?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I think what Dr. Karadzic meant to ask the witness more explicitly is this the report of the working group that you received as prime minister and I think if the answer to that is not clear from the answer he gave at line 4, then perhaps we could ask that again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you were satisfied with the report and whether the working group conveyed and noted everything that was a problem in Srebrenica on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, according to their report, we later on took our moves because we also agreed that the last government session would be devoted to Srebrenica so that we would see what materiel in terms of food, and so on, was needed to appoint certain people to certain positions so that civilian life in Srebrenica could be organised more easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you in any report, this one or some other report, receive information that POWs were shot or that anyone else in Srebrenica was shot?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. McKenna?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3376, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In a telegram dated the 12th of July, where it says that they are available and have been secured, trucks and buses, how did you understand this, that they were already driven there, or how do you interpret this, that they are available, the trucks, I mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: I understand and interpret this that they quickly got in touch over the phone, all the representatives of war staffs from neighbouring municipalities and said what they could offer to the army in order to have the necessary number. That's the way we operated during the war and this is how I interpreted the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did it mean that they were already sent to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: No. It was just that how many there were that we would count on from how many enterprises, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please have a look at P6210. This is an alleged meeting at which supposedly what was discussed was paying for the capturing of Teocak which you denied, and I wish to ask you something, just one sentence so that we could hear your comment. And can we please zoom in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness -- Mr. Karadzic's question, Ms. McKenna, could you remind me of the witness who you cross-examined in the previous time? Who was it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I don't follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The witness you cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Last week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Last week, the previous time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: That was Radojica Mladjenjovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I read out to you, it says, I informed the commander of IBK, General Simic, with this information. The information was received from a reliable source and has not been verified, which I am going to do during my further work and I will later inform you about any new information I receive. What does this tell you, what sort of a document is this, and do you know whether it was determined by verification whether the document was correct or not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: I did not see the lower part on the screen. I am not even familiar with this Mr. Todorovic, and this confirms my words that he's relying himself on some rumours from the town or whoever told him this. It's completely unverified this information. He says reliable but what did they consider reliable from the pre-war UDBA? That was the secret service. He says himself that it's unverified and that in his future work he would verify it. But I said earlier that I had never seen these people as civilians before the war, during the war, or after the war. I didn't know them personally at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now please see, probably has a new number now, 65 ter 11544. Can you please read out loud the last paragraph, 11544, and probably it is now under a different number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6286, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will ask you to read out loud the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: "Asked by the journalists if the SDS would distance itself from the Chetniks in eastern Herzegovina as requested by the president of the Presidency Alija Izetbegovic, the SDS stated the following: We are not an ideological party but a democratic one. Those who declare themselves as Chetniks can find their place in the Serbian Radical Party. We do not advocate any extreme requests."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How does that fit in with the knowledge you had and your experience with our policy towards extremists, whatever they are called?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, just as you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. McKenna [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: That's outside the scope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: What's the problem now? I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. McKenna's objection was that it went beyond the scope of the cross-examination but witness has already answered the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I think that the document has been admitted during the cross-examination. So the Prosecution will be able to refer to it and this is an opportunity for me to offer another document for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The point has been taken. Please move on. But how long do you need to conclude?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Kozic, that I cannot play some of our intercepted conversations, yours and mine, but without playing them I would like to ask you if you know who is Mladen Vukovic of Bileca?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: In any event this is, I believe -- well, perhaps Mr. Karadzic can advise where this arises from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll see.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to see from the intercept what my position was after the press conference and when the journalist asked me what I was saying about the Chetniks in eastern Herzegovina. In the interview, I said that they should stop being Chetniks. That's the link with this document which has been admitted, and it's quite significant because throughout this time we made efforts, it's rather very important for relations with the Muslims and their feeling of security in eastern Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it has been admitted, you can use it in your later submission.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this one hasn't been admitted. Can we have 1D05686, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. McKenna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Kozic answered the question before I had a chance to rise to my feet but this entire topic is outside the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, the topic that he's about to get to is the weapons seizure on the 24th of May, 1991, and what his attitude towards that was, which was first expressed in the news article that was just discussed and is now going to -- was the topic of some conversation during an intercepted conversation between Dr. Karadzic and individual in the same town, Bileca. So that's where we are going with that and I think it's well within the cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In that sense, we allow the accused to proceed. Yes, we have the intercept before us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please see the next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this? Whether these rumours concerning the transport or smuggling of weapons, how did they affect the good neighbourly relations within Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Are you asking me, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a minor incident, and I think that I said in the first part that what confirms that is that in Trebinje and in Ljubinje we had fighters in our battalions who responded to the mobilisation call-up and we lived quite peacefully and in a tolerant way. It was that their extremists wanted to have interparty fights and disputes and the people were frightened and during the first stage they responded in large numbers to mobilisation call-ups and when the Territorial Defence called them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you said fighters, did you have in mind any specific ethnicity? You said you had fighters but you didn't say which fighters.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: In our Ljubinje Battalion, half of the fighters were Muslims, our neighbours. They responded to the call-up and as long as up until 1994, they responded to our call-up.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the speakers please slow down and make a break between questions and answers for the purposes of interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They will never be safer than in eastern Herzegovina. There would be no danger for them and our people should try to calm down, we have reason that the passions, the cockades should calm down a bit. We ask the partisans not to be partisans and we ask the Chetniks not to be the Chetniks, and then the next one, the parties have accepted it but now we have a sort of extremists. It should be a little bit today will go to the Aktiva [phoen], and so on. How does this correspond with the information you had about our position towards our own extremists?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, Mr. President. That was one of the most attractive things that attracted me to you early on, the tolerance that you had. You kept saying to all extremists -- extremely oriented guys in our own ranks that we would not need 1942 when the Chetniks and the partisans divided among themselves into two armies, you said that we would again have 1942 and that now the children of the partisans would be in conflict with the children of the partisans --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down for the purposes of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kozic, could you repeat your answer? You spoke too fast for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And from where you said that was the basis of our soft policy.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: The policy advocated by Mr. Karadzic could be summed up by his speeches at our rallies, where he kept warning our guys who had right-wing leanings or who were fans of Drazan Halovic's [phoen] movement. He used to say to them this, Don't behave in a violent manner, don't be too rough, because we won't get anything by that. Once again, we will be reliving the year 1942, when the anti-fascist front of the Serbs in the then Yugoslavia split into the partisans and the Chetniks. It's only that the situation would be the opposite now, that is to say the descendants of the Chetniks will now threaten the descendants of the partisans, and this position was something that won over the hearts of all the Serbs in Republika Srpska, and that was why in the first elections we won more than 98 per cent of the votes. And Mr. Karadzic, this is a quotation, these were his words: "My children, even the families of those Serbs who are on the communists and reformists lists voted for us."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who were the Muslims in eastern Herzegovina more afraid of in terms of the Serbs, the partisans or the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we will not allow that question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you just tell us whether this -- the weapons in your case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you have more questions, let's do it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it the only trick or deception about the weapons, and what was the outcome in court?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Well, the trial was shifted to Niksic and Podgorica by the army and the police because this was the place of the origin of the act, the misdemeanour, and the trial was completed there. I wasn't attended and no one even invited me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But were you convicted or were you accused or were you indicted?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for coming here to testify, Mr. Kozic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOZIC
utterances.text: Thank you too, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the transcript. I move to tender this into evidence. I meant the intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
